source.title: OnePiece: The Great Route to Generative Recommendation -- A Case Study from Tencent Algorithm Competition
source.authors: Jiangxia Cao; Shuo Yang; Zijun Wang; Qinghai Tan

record.file_problem: Figure 1 is referenced, but its plotted numerical values are not present in the text extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Tests power-law loss scaling in generative recommendation, a different task setting from language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The paper states that InfoNCE and SID losses follow power laws with R² > 0.9, and refers to Figure 1 for the scaling results. It does not provide the plotted loss values or the model-size range in the extracted text. Results in Tables 3 and 5 concern ranking metrics, not loss scaling; they are not recorded as rows here.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own fit of recommendation-model losses (InfoNCE, SID) against model size, with power-law R² > 0.9. This is a new non-language setting with a direct result on the power-law form, so it bears on V5 only.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that semantic ID generation and in-batch InfoNCE can be scaled together in one HSTU+MoE backbone, that both losses follow power laws, and that a collaborative tokenizer reduces item collisions.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales recommendation-task InfoNCE and SID losses in a unified HSTU+MoE architecture; it does not test language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling or compute-optimal allocation.

fits_no_version.finding: In recommendation models, ranking metrics (training Hitrate, SID HR@10) rise monotonically with encoder depth. Tables 3 and 5 cover about 15M–76M parameters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream ranking metrics in generative recommenders improve steadily with model size.

record.problems: The extracted text does not include the numerical loss points or model-size range from Figure 1, and reports no uncertainty estimates or controls for the loss-scaling result.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 3 and 5 report Hitrate and HR@10 across layer configurations, while Table 4 reports validation/test metrics across epochs; these are ranking or evaluation metrics rather than the loss-scaling measures recorded here.

untested.parts: Image/video modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer; scaling in data or compute; scaling across more than one order of magnitude in size; held-out loss.

record.verdict_notes: The scaling evidence rests on one claim of R² > 0.9 and an unextracted figure. The sweeps vary only depth, over under one order of magnitude, with no exponents, uncertainties or held-out confirmation. The Tables 3 and 5 metrics are training-batch averages. The paper cites GPT-4 rather than Kaplan as its scaling-law reference.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation as a function of compute.
Effects of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, and transfer; the extracted text does not establish whether the reported losses are held-out.
Predictability of downstream-task performance from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup or fitting choices, and bending away from a single power law.

rows.subject: OnePiece
rows.operation_detail: Compared InfoNCE loss across model sizes in the unified recommendation architecture.
rows.measure: InfoNCE loss scaling with model size
rows.value: R² > 0.9; numerical loss values are figure only
rows.note: The text explicitly describes the InfoNCE objective as adhering to a power law; the figure's plotted values are unavailable in the extraction.
rows.check: The link and state are fine, but the evidence is thin. The only numbers are R² > 0.9 and the Figure 1 values. The size range is likely the Table 3 depth sweep (0.0152B–0.0573B, about 4x, depth only at D=128), but the text does not confirm this. It is also unclear whether the loss is held-out; Table 3 metrics are training averages.

rows.subject: OnePiece
rows.operation_detail: Compared SID generation loss across model sizes in the unified recommendation architecture.
rows.value: R² > 0.9; numerical loss values are figure only
rows.note: The text explicitly describes the generative SID objective as adhering to a power law; the figure's plotted values are unavailable in the extraction.
rows.check: Same caveats as r1. The size range is probably the Table 5 SID sweep (0.0341B–0.0762B, about 2x, depth only), which is not confirmed for Figure 1. Held-out status is not stated, and no exponents are reported.

relationships.condition: Recommendation InfoNCE and SID losses vs model size, TencentGR-100M, first epoch, small depth-only sweeps
relationships.reason: The authors report both losses fit power laws with R² > 0.9 (r1, r2). The evidence is weak: figure-only values, a narrow size range and an unclear held-out status.
relationships.display_finding: InfoNCE and SID losses both fitted power laws with R²>0.9 over a narrow model-size range, although their held-out status was unclear.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
